title: Infrastructure and IT operations
description: Servers, virtual machines and containers, services, networks, storage, workflows, incidents, changes and runbooks, with where each one runs and what depends on what. Aligned with the configuration-item model of ITIL/CMDB.
standards: ITIL / CMDB configuration items and relationships

entity_types.name: Host
entity_types.description: A physical server or hypervisor node that runs guests or services. Use for: bare-metal machines, Proxmox/ESXi/Kubernetes nodes, NAS and appliances that host workloads. Not for: a VM or container (Guest) or a site (Location). Examples: 'pve-01', 'node-02', 'nas-main'.

entity_types.name: Guest
entity_types.description: A virtual machine or container running on a host. Use for: VMs, LXC and Docker containers identified by name or ID. Not for: the application that runs inside it (Service) or the machine it runs on (Host). Examples: 'LXC 104 vaultwarden', 'VM 100 homeassistant'.

entity_types.name: Service
entity_types.description: A running application or software service that provides something to users or other systems. Use for: web apps, databases, daemons, APIs, SaaS in use. Not for: the machine or container it runs in (Host/Guest) or its domain name (Network). Examples: 'Grafana', 'PostgreSQL', 'Vaultwarden'.

entity_types.name: Workflow
entity_types.description: An automated sequence of steps or a scheduled job. Use for: n8n/Ansible/cron/CI pipelines and backup jobs. Not for: a manual procedure (Runbook). Examples: 'nightly backup job', 'n8n DHCP cleanup'.

entity_types.name: Network
entity_types.description: A network, address space, domain or hostname. Use for: VLANs, subnets, VPNs, DNS names, reverse proxies and ingress endpoints. Not for: a physical site (Location) or a device. Examples: 'VLAN 3 services', 'grafana.example.com', 'Tailscale tailnet'.

entity_types.name: Storage
entity_types.description: A storage pool, volume, share or backup repository. Use for: ZFS pools, NFS/SMB shares, object buckets, PBS datastores. Not for: the server that exports it (Host). Examples: 'pool tank', 'NFS share media', 'datastore main'.

entity_types.name: Incident
entity_types.description: An unplanned interruption or degradation of a service, with its time and impact. Use for: outages, failures, alerts that required action. Not for: planned maintenance (Change). Examples: 'DNS outage 2026-10-12', 'backup failed on node-03'.

entity_types.name: Change
entity_types.description: A planned modification of the infrastructure: upgrade, migration, configuration change, decommissioning. Use for: things that were done on purpose, with a date. Not for: failures (Incident) or general how-tos (Runbook). Examples: 'Migrate Vaultwarden to Docker', 'Upgrade to Debian 13'.

entity_types.name: Runbook
entity_types.description: A documented procedure or recipe to do or fix something. Use for: step-by-step guides, checklists, known fixes. Not for: an automated job (Workflow) or a decision (Decision). Examples: 'How to restore from PBS', 'Fix: restart zigbee bridge'.

entity_types.name: Decision
entity_types.description: A design or operational decision with its rationale. Use for: 'we chose X over Y because Z'. Not for: plans not yet decided. Examples: 'Use Pangolin for public ingress', 'Keep AdGuard on three nodes'.

entity_types.name: Location
entity_types.description: A physical site or place where equipment is installed. Use for: rooms, racks, data centers, regions. Not for: servers (Host) or networks. Examples: 'server room', 'rack U20', 'Hetzner Falkenstein'.

entity_types.name: Organization
entity_types.description: A company or provider outside the infrastructure itself. Use for: vendors, hosting and SaaS providers, ISPs. Not for: the services they provide (Service). Examples: 'Hetzner', 'Cloudflare'.

entity_types.name: Person
entity_types.description: A person involved in operating or using the infrastructure. Not for: teams or providers (Organization). Examples: 'Rafa', 'the on-call engineer'.

entity_types.name: Document
entity_types.description: A manual, specification or note about the infrastructure that can be cited. Not for: a step-by-step procedure (Runbook). Examples: 'UPS manual', 'network diagram'.

entity_types.name: Event
entity_types.description: A dated occurrence that is neither an incident nor a change. Not for: outages (Incident) or planned work (Change). Examples: 'power cut 2026-09-03', 'certificate expiry'.

entity_types.name: Topic
entity_types.description: A subject or concept. LAST RESORT: only when nothing more specific fits. Not for: any host, guest, service, network or storage. Examples: 'high availability'.

edge_types.name: HostedOn
edge_types.description: A guest or service runs on a host, guest or platform (where it lives right now).

edge_types.name: DependsOn
edge_types.description: An entity needs another to work (a service needing a database, a guest needing a storage pool).

edge_types.name: ConnectsTo
edge_types.description: An entity is attached to or reachable through a network.

edge_types.name: Exposes
edge_types.description: A service is reachable through a domain, hostname or ingress.

edge_types.name: Monitors
edge_types.description: A service or workflow watches or alerts about another entity.

edge_types.name: BacksUpTo
edge_types.description: An entity is backed up to a storage target or backup service.

edge_types.name: MigratedTo
edge_types.description: An entity moved from one host or platform to another (record the date).

edge_types.name: CausedBy
edge_types.description: An incident or problem was caused by an entity, change or event.

edge_types.name: ResolvedBy
edge_types.description: An incident was resolved by a change or a runbook.

edge_types.name: Affects
edge_types.description: An incident or change impacts a service, guest or host.

edge_types.name: LocatedAt
edge_types.description: A host or device is installed at a location.

edge_types.name: DecidedBy
edge_types.description: A decision was made by a person or organization.

edge_types.name: Owns
edge_types.description: A person or organization owns or is responsible for an entity.

edge_types.name: MentionedIn
edge_types.description: An entity is referenced in a document.

edge_types.name: RelatesTo
edge_types.description: LAST RESORT. Use only when two entities are clearly associated and no other relation type in the list fits. Never use it when a more specific type applies.

instructions: Infrastructure and IT operations notes. Classify every entity with the MOST SPECIFIC infrastructure type: applications = Service, VM or container = Guest, physical servers and hypervisor nodes = Host, domains/hostnames/VLANs = Network, pools and shares = Storage. Use Organization, Location, Person, Document, Event or Topic only for things that are not infrastructure. Extract HostedOn for every guest or service with a stated host, MigratedTo for moves (with the date), DependsOn for requirements, Exposes for services reachable through a domain, Monitors and BacksUpTo for monitoring and backups, and CausedBy/ResolvedBy/Affects for incidents and changes. Use only the listed relation types and prefer a specific one over RelatesTo.
